title: The Spire of Ironhollow Anew
premise: Jude Nakamura, a smuggler-cartographer whose maps chart the unmapped Thornfell mountains, discovers his own name and tonight's date inked in a century-old book of prophecies hidden in a dead client's belongings. The prophecy foretells a bargain made before his birth: his grandmother sold a sliver of his soul to the Court Beneath the Mountain to save the family, and the debt now comes due. Guided by Sera, a half-fae archivist who once tried to escape the Court herself, Jude descends through the smuggler roads he alone knows to steal his soul-shard back from the Ironhollow court. He succeeds only by offering truth in place of the stolen piece — revealing the Court's own founding lie — and returns to the surface changed, half-mortal and wholly his own, with Sera choosing the sunlit world beside him.
about_author: Yara Brightwater is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons mapping the passes of a mountain range she still refuses to name. She writes fantasy about people who read the landscape the way others read faces, and she insists every map in her books is technically accurate.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. While inventorying a dead smuggler's effects, Jude finds a prophecy book listing tonight's date and his own name. He laughs it off — until the ink shifts to match the exact hour. The emotional beat is uneasy denial: a man who trusts maps above all confronting a text that maps him.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He tests the book against his own records and finds every past entry came true, including his parents' deaths. A hooded stranger in the tavern warns him the Court Beneath the Mountain has 'opened his account.' Fear hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with a letter from his late grandmother in her voice. He finds her hidden ledger: a bargain signed in her blood, a sliver of his soul pawned to save the family from famine. Grief and betrayal braid together as he learns he was collateral before he was born.

chapters.title: Sera of the Stacks
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the Court's surface archive, half-fae archivist Sera recognizes the prophecy's signature and defects with a stolen page, seeking Jude. Her beat is quiet desperation: she has one chance to use an outsider to break a rule she's broken once before.

chapters.title: A Bargain of Directions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sera finds Jude; he refuses until she proves the soul-shard is already failing — his reflection lags, his shadow drifts. They strike an uneasy pact: her knowledge of the Court for his maps of the Thornfell. Trust is transactional and thin.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't on Any Map
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They enter the smuggler roads only he knows, but the mountain has rearranged itself — the Court is rewriting his geography. Jude must navigate by memory and dead reckoning. The beat is vertigo: the expert losing mastery of his own domain.

chapters.title: Tollgate at Duskfall
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At a border toll, a fae customs-warden recognizes Sera as a runaway debtor and demands her name as payment. Jude lies brilliantly to save her — the smuggler's craft turned to loyalty. Sera realizes he's risking his shrinking soul for her.

chapters.title: What the Shadow Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His detached shadow appears at camp, wearing his grandmother's face, and offers to guide him to Ironhollow — for a price to be named later. He accepts, knowing better. The beat is dread wrapped in tenderness: family love weaponized.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. First sight of Ironhollow: a court of iron chandeliers and borrowed memories, where nobles wear souls like jewelry. Sera's old master, the Magistrate of Debts, greets her with terrifying warmth. Her beat is the pull of a gilded cage she once called home.

chapters.title: An Inventory of Jude Nakamura
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Brought before the Magistrate, Jude is appraised like goods: the soul-shard is displayed in a glass reliquary, singing with his grandmother's voice. He must smile, bow, and plan theft under the eyes of beings who taste lies. Suppression as survival.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Second Treason
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Magistrate offers Sera full pardon if she betrays Jude's plan — and reveals he already knows there is one. She accepts, lying with the fluency the Court taught her, then hates herself for how easily it came. The loyalty-vs-truth theme turns inward.

chapters.title: Cartography of a Lie
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude draws a false map of the reliquary vault for Sera to 'sell' to the Court, gambling that they'll trust the traitor's goods. Drawing it, he realizes the vault's geometry matches his grandmother's ledger. The debt has a pattern — and patterns can be broken.

chapters.title: The Night Market of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the Court's black market they buy a forged soul-sigil with the shadow's promised price: one true memory of Jude's grandmother. The beat is bittersweet sacrifice — he pays in the one warm memory he has, and feels it go.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Reliquary Opens
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Using the false map and forged sigil, they reach the reliquary — and find the Court expected them. The shard is real, but touching it floods Jude with the Court's founding memory: the first Magistrate stole the mountain's own name to build Ironhollow. The Court's power rests on a theft older than his debt.

chapters.title: Prisoners of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, in captivity. Separated from Sera, Jude is interrogated by the shadow, revealed as the fragment of himself the Court has been cultivating as an informant. It offers him his soul back if he abandons Sera. He refuses — and learns the refusal itself strengthens what's left of him.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Testimony
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Brought before the Magistrate, Sera 'confesses' — and delivers the false map as evidence, steering the Court's defenses exactly where Jude needs them thin. Her beat is the cost of deception: to save him she must become, convincingly, what the Court always said she was.

chapters.title: The Name Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Escaping via the shadow's reluctant help, Jude descends past the vault to the mountain's root, where the stolen true name of Ironhollow lies buried. He understands the ending of the prophecy at last: the debt can only be paid with a greater truth. Awe and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Everything the Court Owes
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, converging with Jude. As the Court celebrates the 'recovered traitor,' Sera turns her testimony inside out before the assembled nobility, revealing the founding theft. Chaos erupts; the Magistrate moves to unmake her. The beat is a traitor's truth told at the worst possible moment — which is the only moment it counts.

chapters.title: Climax: The Debt Called Due
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jude speaks the mountain's true name aloud in the heart of Ironhollow. The Court's iron unbinds; debts dissolve; the Magistrate, revealed as a hollowed first debtor, crumbles. The reliquary opens freely, but the shard, half-merged with the shadow, must be chosen — whole truth, or comfortable half-soul.

chapters.title: Half of Me, All of Mine
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude takes back the shard and, in a final act, releases the shadow — his grandmother's echo — to rest, forgiving the bargain she made. He walks out of Ironhollow half-mortal, fully himself. The beat is grief transmuted into inheritance: he keeps her love, not her debt.

chapters.title: The Mapmaker's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Above ground, Sera faces her own ledger: the Court is gone, but her old debts to the surface world remain. Jude offers her a blank page — a map with no roads yet. She chooses the unmapped life. Quiet, earned joy after the fall.

chapters.title: Epilogue: First Light on Thornfell
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, one year later. Jude burns the prophecy book — its last pages now blank — and pins a new map to his workshop wall: the Thornfell, redrawn with roads only he and Sera know. His reflection no longer lags. The final beat is ownership of one's story: some things are inherited, and some are chosen.
